question.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 & -2 \\ -2 & -1 & -2 & 5 \\ 1 & 3 & -1 & 2 \\ -1 & -2 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries above and below ${a}_{33}$ equal to zero.*
question.worked_solution:
Let's make entries above and below ${a}_{33}=-1$ equal to zero using elementary row operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 & -2 \\ -2 & -1 & -2 & 5 \\ 1 & 3 & -1 & 2 \\ -1 & -2 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+{R}_{3} \\ {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{3} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+3{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 6 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & -7 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 & -1 & 2 \\ 2 & 7 & 0 & 8\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $3$rd column, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & 6 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & -7 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 & -1 & 2 \\ 2 & 7 & 0 & 8\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-1)\cdot (-1)^{3+3}|\begin{aligned}2 & 6 & 0 \\ -4 & -7 & 1 \\ 2 & 7 & 8\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}2 & 6 & 0 \\ -4 & -7 & 1 \\ 2 & 7 & 8\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$
